title: Reading the carbamazepine and abacavir labels

segs.text: Section twenty eight. Carbamazepine and abacavir: one gene, two variants. Carbamazepine, brand name Tegretol, is one of the older antiepileptics still in use. Abacavir, brand name Ziagen, is an antiretroviral for H I V, a nucleoside analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitor. Both carry an H L A B warning, for a different variant of the same gene, and the hypersensitivity shows up in a different place.

Unlike trastuzumab, there is no tumor. The risk comes from H L A alleles the patient inherited, so the patient's own D N A is genotyped. The variants raise the risk of hypersensitivity; they do not make the drug less effective or change the dose.

Carbamazepine has two genes to check: H L A B, variant star fifteen oh two, and H L A A, variant star thirty one oh one, which the label now adds. So H L A B alone no longer covers the risk. Either variant significantly increases the risk of a severe skin reaction, Stevens Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis, S J S or T E N, which can be fatal. The boxed warning says patients with ancestry in genetically at risk populations should be screened for H L A B star fifteen oh two before starting.

Abacavir goes with H L A B star fifty seven oh one. The problem was first seen as massive skin reactions, like carbamazepine; the labeling later changed to a hypersensitivity reaction involving multiple organs, listing multi organ failure and anaphylaxis, so it is not skin only. The label says to screen all patients for star fifty seven oh one before starting or restarting abacavir, and the drug is contraindicated in patients who test positive.

She said, They both cause a risk for a hypersensitivity reaction, but carbamazepine is located in the skin, and for abacavir, it's a whole organ hypersensitivity reaction. One negative H L A B test does not clear both drugs: a patient negative for fifteen oh two may still carry fifty seven oh one. H L A B star fifty eight oh one and H L A D R B one star fifteen oh one belong to neither; those go with allopurinol and amoxicillin clavulanate.
